modules.summary: Pericardial layers, sinuses, innervation, and tamponade.

The transverse and oblique sinuses have different surgical relationships.
Phrenic nerves descend on the fibrous pericardium.

retrieval.prompt: Which attachment most directly fixes the fibrous pericardium inferiorly?
In the displayed heart-wall diagram, which layer is identical to the visceral layer of serous pericardium?
During cardiac surgery, a clamp is passed behind the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk. Which pericardial space is being used?

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: External heart anatomy
modules.summary: Apex, base, surfaces, and chambers seen from external views.
keyPoints: The left ventricle forms the apex.
The left atrium forms most of the base.
The right ventricle forms most of the sternocostal surface.

retrieval.prompt: Which chamber forms the apex of the adult heart?
Which chamber forms most of the posterior base of the heart?
In an anterior view of the heart, which chamber occupies most of the sternocostal surface?

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: Internal chambers and valves
modules.summary: Atrial and ventricular landmarks and valve apparatus.
keyPoints: The moderator band carries the right bundle branch.
Chordae prevent AV valve prolapse rather than opening valves.
Coronary ostia arise in the aortic sinuses.

retrieval.prompt: Which structure carries part of the right bundle branch to the anterior papillary muscle?
Why is the left ventricular myocardium substantially thicker than the right ventricular myocardium?
retrieval.answer: It pumps against the higher resistance of the systemic circulation

retrieval.prompt: In the superior valve view, the right and left coronary arteries arise from which structures?
retrieval.answer: Corresponding right and left aortic sinuses

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: Coronary circulation
modules.summary: Major coronary arteries, dominance, and venous drainage.
modules.sourceLocator: Heart 2.pptx slide 8; Heart 3.pptx slide 11; Gray's Anatomy 42e local PDF pp. 1709, 1713
keyPoints: The anterior interventricular artery runs with the great cardiac vein.
Dominance is defined by origin of the posterior interventricular artery.
The coronary sinus opens into the right atrium.

retrieval.prompt: Which vein most consistently accompanies the anterior interventricular artery in the anterior interventricular sulcus?
In a right-dominant coronary circulation, the posterior interventricular artery usually arises from which artery?
Which observation establishes that a heart is left dominant?
retrieval.answer: The posterior interventricular artery arises from the circumflex artery

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: Mediastinum and great vessels
modules.summary: Cardiac plexuses, aortic arch structures, recurrent laryngeal relation, azygos arch, and posterior mediastinal contents.
keyPoints: The superficial cardiac plexus lies anterior and inferior to the aortic arch.
The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops below the aortic arch.
The azygos vein arches over the right lung root.

retrieval.prompt: In panel A of the displayed mediastinal diagram, which plexus is labeled on the anterior aspect of the aortic arch?
Which nerve loops beneath the aortic arch adjacent to the ligamentum arteriosum?
The azygos vein enters the superior vena cava after arching over which structure?

modules.subject: physiology
modules.title: Hemodynamics
modules.summary: Ohm, Poiseuille, Laplace, velocity, Reynolds, and Bernoulli relationships.
modules.sourceLocator: Cairculatory System 1.pptx slides 16-17, 27-28; Cairculatory System 2.pptx slides 5-9; Cairculatory System 3.pptx slides 7, 13-14; Cairculatory System 4.pptx slide 5
keyPoints: Flow equals pressure difference divided by resistance.
Resistance is inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power.
Velocity is inversely related to total cross-sectional area.

retrieval.prompt: If the pressure gradient across an organ doubles while vascular resistance remains constant, what happens to blood flow?
A small artery's radius doubles with all other variables unchanged. According to Poiseuille's relationship, flow becomes approximately how many times greater?
At a fixed pressure gradient and vessel geometry, an increase in blood viscosity has what immediate effect?

modules.subject: physiology
modules.title: Cardiac cycle, conduction, and pressure
modules.summary: Valve events, pressure-volume phases, pulse pressure, compliance, and myocardial electrophysiology.
modules.sourceLocator: Cairculatory System 3.pptx slides 8-12; Guyton 15e local PDF pp. 124, 131-136
keyPoints: All valves are closed during isovolumic phases.
The SA node normally initiates the heartbeat.
The ventricular action-potential plateau prolongs refractoriness.

retrieval.prompt: The displayed slide marks the interval from mitral-valve closure to aortic-valve opening. Which statement is correct during this interval?
retrieval.answer: Ventricular pressure rises while volume remains constant

retrieval.prompt: Which valve events bound isovolumic relaxation of the left ventricle?
retrieval.answer: Aortic closure followed by mitral opening

retrieval.prompt: A patient's arterial pressure is 120/80 mmHg. What is the pulse pressure?

modules.subject: physiology
modules.title: Microcirculation and edema
modules.summary: Vascular volume, capillary exchange, Starling forces, edema, and venous return.
keyPoints: Capillary velocity is low because total cross-sectional area is high.
Hydrostatic pressure favors filtration.
One-way venous valves support the muscle pump.

retrieval.prompt: Which part of the systemic circulation contains the largest fraction of blood volume at rest?
The course slide shows capillary blood velocity far below arterial velocity. Which structural property explains this?
retrieval.answer: Very large total capillary cross-sectional area

retrieval.prompt: Which capillary type is most characteristic of skeletal muscle and has an uninterrupted endothelium and basement membrane?

modules.subject: physiology
modules.title: Reflex and local circulatory regulation
modules.summary: Baroreceptors, chemoreceptors, active/reactive hyperemia, metabolites, and humoral control.
modules.sourceLocator: Cairculatory System 4.pptx slides 16-20; Cairculatory System 5.pptx slides 7-8, 11, 15
keyPoints: Carotid sinus afferents travel in CN IX.
Active hyperemia follows increased metabolism.
Angiotensin II and vasopressin are vasoconstrictors.

retrieval.prompt: The displayed reflex slide shows carotid sinus afferents reaching the medulla through which cranial nerve?
A sudden rise in arterial pressure increases carotid sinus firing. What is the immediate integrated response?
retrieval.answer: Reduced sympathetic and increased parasympathetic activity

retrieval.prompt: Which combination most strongly stimulates peripheral arterial chemoreceptors?
retrieval.answer: Low arterial O2, high CO2, and increased H+

modules.subject: physiology
modules.title: Special circulations and integrated responses
modules.summary: Pulmonary, cerebral, coronary, exercise, and hemorrhage physiology.
modules.sourceLocator: Cairculatory System 5.pptx slides 4, 6; Cairculatory System 6.pptx slides 5-15
keyPoints: Pulmonary vascular resistance is much lower than systemic resistance.
Local metabolism is the main controller of coronary flow.
Hemorrhage unloads baroreceptors and increases sympathetic activity.

retrieval.prompt: Systemic and pulmonary circulations have the same cardiac output. Why is pulmonary arterial pressure much lower?
retrieval.answer: Pulmonary vascular resistance is much lower

retrieval.prompt: Which mechanism is especially important for matching cerebral blood flow to local neuronal activity?
Why is left coronary flow greatest during ventricular diastole?
retrieval.answer: Systolic myocardial compression impedes intramural vessels

modules.subject: physiology
modules.title: Red-cell physiology
modules.summary: Erythropoiesis, maturation, iron handling, and red-cell lifespan.
keyPoints: Renal erythropoietin rises with hypoxia.
Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency causes failure of normal erythroid precursor maturation.
Senescent red cells are removed by macrophages.

retrieval.prompt: What is the most important physiological signal increasing erythropoietin production?
Deficiency of vitamin B12 or folate produces megaloblastic anemia primarily by causing which erythrocyte-development problem?
retrieval.answer: Failure of normal erythroid precursor maturation

retrieval.prompt: Which pairing correctly matches an iron-binding protein with its principal role?

modules.subject: physiology
modules.title: Hemostasis and coagulation
modules.summary: Platelet plug formation, coagulation pathways, vitamin K, and fibrinolysis.
keyPoints: vWF mediates platelet adhesion to exposed collagen.
Tissue factor initiates the extrinsic pathway.
tPA activates plasminogen.

retrieval.prompt: What is the correct early sequence after a small blood vessel is injured?
retrieval.answer: Vasoconstriction, platelet plug formation, then coagulation

retrieval.prompt: Which plasma protein is most important for platelet adhesion to exposed subendothelial collagen?
Which substances released by activated platelets recruit and activate additional platelets?

modules.subject: histology
modules.title: Histology of the heart
modules.summary: Endocardium, myocardium, epicardium, cardiac skeleton, and Purkinje fibers.
keyPoints: Purkinje fibers are pale and glycogen-rich.
The epicardium is visceral serous pericardium.
Dense connective tissue forms the cardiac skeleton.

retrieval.prompt: Which tissue directly lines the chambers and valves of the heart?
Which heart-wall layer contains the contractile cardiac muscle responsible for pumping?
Which feature is most characteristic of epicardium?
retrieval.answer: Mesothelium over connective tissue containing vessels, nerves, and fat

modules.subject: histology
modules.title: Arteries and vessel-wall organization
modules.summary: Tunics, elastic and muscular arteries, and arterioles.
keyPoints: Endothelium lines the tunica intima.
Elastic arteries contain many elastic lamellae in the media.
Arterioles have only one or a few smooth-muscle layers.

retrieval.prompt: Which cell type forms the luminal surface of all blood vessels?
Which component usually dominates the tunica media of a muscular artery?
Which histological feature best identifies an elastic artery?
retrieval.answer: Numerous fenestrated elastic lamellae in the tunica media

modules.subject: histology
modules.title: Microvasculature
modules.summary: Capillary types, pericytes, metarterioles, and postcapillary venules.
keyPoints: Continuous capillaries have tight junctions.
Fenestrations facilitate exchange.
Postcapillary venules are major sites of leukocyte exit.

retrieval.prompt: In the displayed comparison, which feature identifies a continuous capillary?
retrieval.answer: Uninterrupted endothelium with tight junctions and continuous basal lamina

retrieval.prompt: Fenestrated capillaries are especially common in which site?
Which combination best characterizes a sinusoidal capillary?
retrieval.answer: Wide irregular lumen, large endothelial gaps, and discontinuous basal lamina

modules.subject: histology
modules.title: Veins and lymphatic vessels
modules.summary: Venous wall organization, valves, and lymphatic capillary structure.
keyPoints: Large veins have prominent adventitia.
Venous valves are folds of the intima.
Lymphatic capillaries begin blindly and lack a continuous basal lamina.

retrieval.prompt: Venous valves are folds of which vessel layer?
Which wall feature is especially prominent in a large vein such as the vena cava?
retrieval.answer: Thick adventitia with longitudinal smooth-muscle bundles

retrieval.prompt: Which feature favors entry of interstitial fluid into lymphatic capillaries?
retrieval.answer: Overlapping endothelial flaps anchored to surrounding connective tissue

retrieval.prompt: The right horn of the sinus venosus is incorporated into the right atrium to form which region?

modules.subject: embryology
modules.title: Atrial, AV, and ventricular septation
modules.summary: Septum primum/secundum, endocardial cushions, and ventricular septum.
modules.sourceLocator: Langman 15e, Chapter 13, local OCR PDF pp. 203-216
keyPoints: The ostium secundum forms within septum primum.
The septum primum becomes the valve of the foramen ovale.
Endocardial cushions divide the AV canal.

retrieval.prompt: The ostium primum normally closes when septum primum fuses with which structures?
How does the ostium secundum form?
retrieval.answer: Programmed cell death creates perforations in the upper septum primum

modules.subject: embryology
modules.title: Outflow tract and congenital defects
modules.summary: Neural crest, conotruncal septation, semilunar valves, and major malformations.
modules.sourceLocator: Langman 15e, Chapter 13, local OCR PDF pp. 214-219
keyPoints: Neural crest cells contribute to conotruncal ridges.
Failure of spiral septation causes transposition.
Anterior displacement produces tetralogy of Fallot.

retrieval.prompt: Cardiac neural crest cells contribute directly to which structure?
retrieval.answer: Conotruncal ridges forming the aorticopulmonary septum

retrieval.prompt: Transposition of the great arteries most directly results from which developmental error?
retrieval.answer: Failure of the aorticopulmonary septum to spiral

retrieval.prompt: In the displayed defect, which single developmental displacement underlies tetralogy of Fallot?
retrieval.answer: Anterior displacement of the conotruncal septum

retrieval.prompt: Which pairing correctly matches a fourth aortic arch derivative?
